items.bold: US APACHE AH-64 HELICOPTER SHOT DOWN by Iranian Shahed drone over Strait of Hormuz overnight Mon-Tue. Both crew rescued by US sea drone — first-ever military sea drone rescue. US LAUNCHED STRIKES ON IRAN 5PM ET Tuesday.
items.text: CBS News, Bloomberg, NPR, CBC (June 9): An Iranian armed Shahed drone struck a US Army AH-64 Apache helicopter patrolling over the Strait of Hormuz overnight Monday, downing the aircraft. Both crew members were rescued by a US Navy surface drone — the first-ever sea drone rescue in US military history — and transported to safety by helicopter. Both pilots were safe and uninjured. Trump confirmed Iran shot it down: 'I have just been informed by our Great Military that last night the Iranians shot down one of our highly sophisticated Apache Helicopters while patrolling over the Strait of Hormuz. Nevertheless, the United States must, of necessity, respond to this attack.' CENTCOM launched 'self-defence strikes' against Iran at 5PM ET Tuesday (approx 2:30AM IST Wednesday): 'The mission is a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression.' Iran has not officially claimed responsibility; Iran's IRIB reported no offensive military operations were carried out in the strait in the last 24 hours. Iran FM Araghchi said foreign forces near Iran's territory 'are at constant risk' and after the strikes: 'Iran will leave no attack or threat unanswered.'

items.bold: TRUMP: Deal 'in two or three days' Tuesday morning. Then Apache response. VP VANCE to CBS: 'Very close to achieving a deal good for the long term. But we still got some wood to chop.'
items.text: CNN, CBS News (June 9): Trump's Tuesday was a study in compressed contradictions. In the morning he told reporters a deal could be reached 'in two or three days.' Hours later he confirmed Iran shot down the Apache and the US 'must respond.' VP Vance told CBS that despite the latest exchange: 'Right now, I feel that we are in a position to get a deal that is good for the United States economically and that really does deal with the Iranian nuclear program, not just now, not just while Donald Trump is president, but for the long term. That's the goal of the policy. And I think we're very close to achieving that goal. But we still got some wood to chop.' The Vance framing is important: the US is not abandoning negotiations — it views military strikes as parallel to, not instead of, diplomacy. The deal framework is still alive. The question is how many more strikes it can absorb.

items.bold: IRAN FM ARAGHCHI: 'Foreign forces near our territory are at constant risk.' After US strikes: 'Iran will leave no attack or threat unanswered.' Iran did not officially claim Apache shootdown.
items.text: CBC, CNBC (June 9): Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi issued a warning before the US strikes: 'Foreign forces in proximity to our territory are at constant risk on account of their own human errors, plain accidents, or potentially being caught in crossfire.' After CENTCOM launched its retaliatory strikes, Iran fired missiles and drones toward US targets in the region, and Araghchi stated: 'Iran will leave no attack or threat unanswered. Leave our region if you want to be safe.' Iran's state broadcaster IRIB notably reported that 'no offensive military operations had been carried out in the strait in the last 24 hours' — Iran did not officially claim the Apache shootdown, leaving open the possibility it was an accident or incident rather than deliberate attack. This ambiguity is important: it gives both sides an exit ramp. CENTCOM used the word 'self-defence strikes' — proportional language suggesting containment, not escalation.

items.bold: DEAL STILL ALIVE: Both sides claim willingness. Vance 'very close.' Trump '2-3 days' (before Apache). Pakistan mediation continuing. Iran UN ambassador optimistic. OPEC+ +188k bpd July.
items.text: CNN, CBS News, CBC (June 9): Despite the Apache shootdown and US retaliatory strikes, the deal framework remains nominally alive. Trump said '2-3 days' Tuesday morning. military.d: CBS News, Bloomberg, NPR, CBC (June 9): An Iranian armed Shahed drone struck a US Army AH-64 Apache helicopter patrolling over the Strait of Hormuz overnight Monday, bringing it down. It was the first US aircraft lost to hostile fire in the conflict. Both crew members were rescued by a US Navy surface (sea) drone — the first-ever such rescue in US military history — and both pilots were safe and uninjured. Trump confirmed on Truth Social: 'I have just been informed by our Great Military that last night the Iranians shot down one of our highly sophisticated Apache Helicopters while patrolling over the Strait of Hormuz. There were two pilots involved, both are safe and uninjured. Nevertheless, the United States must, of necessity, respond to this attack.' CENTCOM launched self-defence strikes at 5PM ET Tuesday at Trump's direction: 'The mission is a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression.' Iran IRIB reported 'no offensive military operations in the strait' in the last 24 hours — Iran did not officially claim the Apache shootdown, leaving open whether it was deliberate or a collision. Iran FM Araghchi: 'Foreign forces near our territory are at constant risk on account of their own human errors, plain accidents, or potentially being caught in crossfire.' After US strikes: 'Iran will leave no attack or threat unanswered. Leave our region if you want to be safe.'

military.t: TRUMP: Deal 'In Two or Three Days' Tuesday Morning. VP VANCE: 'Very Close to Achieving a Deal Good for the Long Term — But Still Got Some Wood to Chop.' Deal Framework Still Alive Despite Apache-Strike Cycle.
military.d: CNN, CBS News (June 9): Trump told reporters Tuesday morning that a deal to end the war could be reached 'in two or three days' — hours before announcing the Apache shootdown and US retaliation. VP Vance told CBS: 'Right now, I feel that we are in a position to get a deal that is good for the United States economically and that really does deal with the Iranian nuclear program, not just now, not just while Donald Trump is president, but for the long term. That's the goal of the policy. And I think we're very close to achieving that goal. But we still got some wood to chop. We're going to keep doing it.' The US administration is explicitly framing military strikes and diplomatic negotiations as parallel processes, not mutually exclusive. Iran's UN ambassador had expressed hope for a final agreement. Pakistan PM Shehbaz had said 'final objective just about to be achieved.' The deal framework is still alive — the Apache-strike cycle is the 'wood to chop.'

military.d: Trading Economics, Investing.com, Goodreturns (June 9-10): Brent fell 3.42% to $91.11 on Tuesday as markets priced in Iran ending military operations against Israel after Monday's exchanges. This was before the overnight Apache shootdown and US retaliatory strikes. Brent is opening at approximately $94.15 on Wednesday — a $3 overnight rebound driven by the new escalation. The 10-day pattern: every new military exchange drives Brent up $3-6, then diplomatic re-engagement partially retraces it. OPEC+ approved another +188,000 bpd output increase for July — insufficient to offset Hormuz closure but a signal. Iran ambassador to Moscow maintained that Hormuz will open under new Iran-Oman conditions including a transit fee. Fresh Chinese crude import data showed Asia's top consumer is running on inventories rather than overseas purchases since the conflict began. For India: at Brent $91-94, OMC diesel under-recovery Rs25-32/L. Fourth hike pressure if Brent holds $95+.

(4) Allow US to UNEARTH AND DESTROY enriched uranium buried under rubble. Trump HAS NOT SIGNED MOU. UBS (Thursday note): "little evidence of short-term improvement in vessel traffic or energy flows." Crude loadings inside Gulf "EXTREMELY LOW." US GAS PRICES: fell 14 CENTS since $4.56/gallon peak — biggest one-day drop since November 2008 Great Recession. IRAN: will only discuss nuclear clauses ONCE Phase 1 MOU cemented. BESSENT: declined to confirm deal details. Thursday: Iran ballistic missiles toward Kuwait intercepted. IRGC warning shots at 4 vessels. India: Brent $92 = Rs 2.3L Cr annual import bill saving vs April $126 peak. OMC near-breakeven on petrol. Month-end Friday. West Asia War Day 91.

DAY 90 THU 8:15AM IST. 60-DAY MOU REACHED BY NEGOTIATORS — extend ceasefire + start nuclear negotiations. TRUMP STILL HAS TO APPROVE. Axios confirmed. CNBC confirmed. IRAN STATE TV: Tehran agreed draft MOU — Hormuz to pre-war levels — BUT Iran AND OMAN manage traffic. WHITE HOUSE: "COMPLETE FABRICATION." TRUMP: "no nation will control shipping" through Hormuz. US-IRAN EXCHANGED FIRE EARLY THURSDAY (CNN 16min ago): US struck Iranian drones + launch site near Hormuz. IRGC fired WARNING SHOTS at FOUR VESSELS near Hormuz (passing "without prior coordination or authorization"). IRAN launched BALLISTIC MISSILES TOWARD KUWAIT — intercepted by CENTCOM. IRGC targeted US AIR BASE at 4:50 AM local time. BRENT: $93.71 Wednesday close (-58 cents) — lowest since mid-March. Rebounding Thursday on fresh fighting. HOCHSTEIN: "No matter what — Iranians will control Hormuz for foreseeable future. Doesn't even matter what the deal says." India Thursday: binary. Trump signs = Brent $85-88, Nifty +800-1,000. Trump rejects = Brent $100+, Nifty -300-400. West Asia War Day 90.

assessment.headline: DAY 102, 7:45AM WED: APACHE HELICOPTER DOWNED BY IRANIAN SHAHED DRONE OVER HORMUZ. BOTH CREW RESCUED (FIRST US SEA DRONE RESCUE EVER). US LAUNCHED RETALIATORY STRIKES 5PM ET TUE. IRAN: 'WILL LEAVE NO ATTACK UNANSWERED.' BRENT $94.15 WED OPEN ($91.11 TUE CLOSE). NIFTY TUE: 23,242 (+0.52%). VANCE: 'VERY CLOSE TO DEAL. MORE WOOD TO CHOP.'
assessment.body:
Wednesday 7:45 AM IST. Day 102.
The most compressed escalation-diplomacy cycle of the war: 24 hours.

WHAT HAPPENED (Day 101 evening → Day 102 morning)
Iranian Shahed armed drone struck US Army AH-64 Apache over Strait of Hormuz.
Both crew rescued by US sea drone — first-ever military sea drone rescue.
Trump: 'Iran shot down one of our Apache Helicopters. US must respond.'
CENTCOM: launched self-defence strikes on Iran 5PM ET Tuesday.
'Proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression.'
Iran FM Araghchi: 'Iran will leave no attack or threat unanswered.'

WHAT HAPPENED THE SAME DAY (before Apache news)
Trump told reporters: deal could be reached 'in two or three days.'
VP Vance to CBS: 'Very close to achieving a deal good for the long term.
But we still got some wood to chop.'
Nifty: recovered +0.52% to 23,242. Sensex +0.54% to 73,919.
Brent fell 3.42% to $91.11 on de-escalation signals. 

BRENT OVERNIGHT WHIPSAW
$91.11 Tuesday close → $94.15 Wednesday open = +$3 overnight.
Pattern: every military exchange = +$3-6 spike, then partial retrace.
The market has learned this cycle. Brent is not going to $110 again
unless there is a true, sustained escalation beyond 'proportional' strikes.

THE DEAL FRAMEWORK — STILL ALIVE
Vance framing: strikes and negotiations are parallel, not exclusive.
Iran did not officially claim Apache shootdown. Left the exit ramp open.
Pakistan mediation continuing. Iran UN ambassador optimistic.
'Two or three days' from Trump = deal possible by Thursday-Friday.

FOR INDIA
Nifty support 23,000-23,100 held Monday. 
Tuesday recovery (+0.52%) shows DII support and domestic resilience.
Wednesday open: gap-down likely but smaller than Monday (-273 Gift gap).
Brent $91-94 range = OMC under-recovery Rs25-32/L diesel.
Fourth hike avoidable if Brent stays below Rs95.
Watch Vance + Trump statements through Wednesday for deal timeline.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.

timeline.tag: WAR BEGINS. US-Israel strike Iran. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed. Hormuz closed within hours.
Hormuz near-total closure confirmed. Brent spiked to $120 briefly. India emergency measures begin.
Brent $108. First India fuel hike (petrol +Rs6/L, diesel +Rs5/L). PM Modi: use energy with restraint.
CEASEFIRE AGREED — US-Iran 2-week pause. Brent fell 16% to $92. Sensex +3,500 pts gap-up. Hormuz nominally reopening.
CEASEFIRE DAY 1. Strait of Hormuz declared open for safe passage. Both crew rescued. Diplomacy begins.
US NAVAL BLOCKADE imposed on Iran ports. Dual blockade. Ceasefire extended indefinitely by Trump.
Second India fuel hike (petrol +Rs5, diesel +Rs4). Islamabad talks collapse. Iran rejects MOU.
Sensex +232 to 75,415. Nifty +65 to 23,719. Week 12 close. Rubio: tentative progress. Iran uranium stays.
TRUMP: deal largely negotiated. RUBIO: days away. PGSA controlled zone graphic. Brent $100.
Trump edited MOU — new uranium/Hormuz demands 'not received well' in Tehran. Iran denied deal. US Defense Secretary combat-ready.
ESCALATION: US struck Qeshm Island. Iran retaliated — 13 missiles + 17 drones at Kuwait + Bahrain. Kuwait Airport hit: 1 Indian killed. Iran halted mediators. House war powers 215-208.
Nifty 23,355 (-0.22%). Sensex 74,219 (-0.17%). Trump: deal 'over the weekend.' Iran halted mediators. US seeks written nuclear commitments. LPG third hike: Rs941.50.
Iran fired 7 ballistic missiles at Kuwait+Bahrain. CENTCOM intercepted 6. Oman terminal explosion. Hezbollah rejected US ceasefire. RBI held 5.25%, 5-pronged FII plan. US S&P -2.64%.

IRAN FIRED MISSILES AT ISRAEL overnight — all intercepted. Israel struck Mahshahr petrochemical complex (first energy strike since ceasefire). Nifty -1.04% (-244 pts). Sensex -719 pts. BSE -Rs6.31T. Brent $97+ intraday → $94.25 close.

IRAN-ISRAEL PAUSE. Trump: 'Both sides want immediate ceasefire.' Iran willing to stop if Israel stops. Pakistan Naqvi letter to Khamenei. Nifty recovered +0.52%. Brent fell 3.42% to $91.11 on de-escalation signals. Vance: 'very close to deal.'

APACHE AH-64 HELICOPTER SHOT DOWN by Iranian Shahed drone over Hormuz overnight. Both crew rescued by sea drone (first-ever US military sea drone rescue). US launched retaliatory strikes 5PM ET Tue. Iran: 'will leave no attack unanswered.' Brent $94.15 Wed open. Vance: 'very close to deal — more wood to chop.'
